description: Twelve-factor settings read through django-environ, which is how most Django projects written since about 2018 are configured and which none of the other fixtures cover. Nothing here is a literal: every value arrives from the environment, so the source alone cannot say what any deployment will actually do. The fixture holds two things in tension. Defects must survive the indirection -- a wrong fallback is still a wrong fallback when it is spelled env.bool(..., default=True) -- and they must arrive at *lower confidence* than the same defect written as a literal, because the operator may well have set the variable. DJS-001 and DJS-013 are pinned at tentative here and at certain or firm in vulnerable_project, and that gap is the thing this fixture is really guarding. DJS-003 stays at firm because the fallback is startproject's own placeholder key, which is published in the Django tutorial and is a specific known value rather than an inference. The controls are the more valuable half and there are more of them: env.db() parses a URL the source never contains, so DJS-004 and DJS-022 must stay silent rather than guess; EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD is required with no default, which is the correct way to hold a credential and must not be punished by a rule that matches on the name; and SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE are read with no inline default at all, so the only way to know they are on is to read the schema passed to Env(). A tool that fires on those idioms fires on the projects that got this right, and gets uninstalled by them.
